messages.message: The FWHM could not be applied to the detector: {1}
The FWHM equation on the FWHM tab has no coefficients, so the detector kept the FWHM it already had. Use "Fit FWHM" there, or enter the coefficients by hand.
No foreground spectrum is loaded, so there is nothing to fit the FWHM to; you can still edit the equation below by hand.
This detector was imported for its geometry only, so it has no efficiency yet. Generate a response on the Monte Carlo tab to give it one.
Could not build an efficiency curve from the generated response: {1}

How this far-field detector answers off-axis, near-field and uncertainty-aware queries.

  • Flat Disk - the classic far-field model: efficiency is the on-axis curve scaled by solid angle, with an abstract energy-correlated uncertainty you edit as a covariance matrix. No geometry is modeled.
  • Geometry Modeled - a Monte-Carlo response, built from the detector geometry below and grounded to the measured efficiency points, supplies the distance/angle dependence and its own finer uncertainty.

Switching a geometry-modeled detector back to Flat Disk detaches its response on "Use" (you will be asked to confirm).

The detector's measured efficiency points, which the Activity/Shielding fit can fold into its results. Edit each point below - its energy, absolute efficiency, and the statistical and certificate uncertainties on that efficiency (points sharing a source are treated as sharing their certificate uncertainty). (A Monte-Carlo-characterized response supplies its own, finer, uncertainty and overrides these points.)

The detector's energy-node covariance matrix, which the Activity/Shielding fit can fold into its results. The diagonal is the 1-sigma fractional uncertainty (%) at each energy, and the off-diagonal is the correlation between energies. Add or remove energy nodes below. (if you change to a geometry-modeled detector efficiency, this matrix will be ignored and not used)
The covariance energies must be distinct; two or more were equal, so the uncertainty was not changed.
The covariance could not be applied, so the uncertainty was not changed: {1}
The regenerated response derives its uncertainty from the measured points, not from a hand-edited covariance matrix.
Switching to Flat Disk removes the geometry-modeled Monte-Carlo response and reverts this detector to the flat-disk far-field model. Continue?
You have edits that the currently generated response does not reflect. Regenerate it from the current geometry and points before using this detector?
Tip: after choosing "Use", you can download this detector as an XML file or a QR code (buttons on the Detector Select dialog), or find it again later under the "Previous" tab of Detector Select.
